notes.title: THE KING OF FIGHTERS XV to be updated on December 12!
notes.notes:
THE KING OF FIGHTERS XV to be updated on December 12
with balance adjustments and special DLC: MATURE and VICE! 
An Ultimate Edition with all DLC characters will also be available!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41117142/62626e29a0f0584a6beb37ae93af6a9c5b873599.jpg[/img]

[b]Trailer: Special DLC “MATURE” & “VICE”
[/b]https://youtu.be/-rcrRSQvzwU

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41117142/de65e1910e16bf018d63fd567c28c1be7a8e8f31.jpg[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41117142/8a34548475c449bfc0479a06c537c9e8dc5fca96.jpg[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41117142/3b4792e1d2cbc27f90d08a79badd24a327458371.jpg[/img]
[b]MATURE[/b]
Mature once counted herself among the Hakkesshu—eight fervent acolytes plotting the resurrection of the divine Orochi (the so-called “will of the earth”). The cruel beauty is fast and fluid in her offense, lacerating opponents with razor-sharp strikes. Her coldhearted realism is a far cry from Vice’s own personality. (VA: Yu Shimamura)


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41117142/f4264a12a754e6037ddf6e168d97fe3791a6fd23.jpg[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41117142/f43308a3b257c58e2d31f0a3e36c3a9cb06a6ac9.jpg[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41117142/4f446e26f76d3b16e64040732b5b9d8f371800b0.jpg[/img]
[b]VICE
[/b]Like Mature, Vice was once one of the Hakkesshu—loyal followers who sought to revive the dreaded Orochi. Her frail stature masks a decidedly violent ruthlessness, which comes to the fore in the way she fights: unbridled strength and brutal throws. Vice is intrigued by Iori Yagami, who carries Orochi blood in his veins. (VA: Mayumi Saco)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41117142/e7a4eda9b17af0d456aae7b55f919781ef5a9fe2.jpg[/img]
[b]Balance adjustments for all characters!
[/b]Alongside the December 12 arrival of special DLC fighters MATURE and VICE, the game will receive a host of balance adjustments across the board. Get ready to experience KOF XV like never before!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41117142/e5047c1e5f60487c5d0548dc7424b1d2b0e42642.jpg[/img]
[b]Announcing the KOF XV Ultimate Edition:
A new bundle featuring every single DLC character on the roster![/b]
Arriving on December 12 as a digital release, the KOF XV Ultimate Edition bundles the base game with all 20 paid DLC characters (including the upcoming MATURE and VICE) and the two DLC costumes—for a massive roster of 61 fighters in total! And that’s not all: the KOF XV Standard Edition and Team Passes also pack a new punch with an unbeatable new price. If you haven’t embarked on your journey to become the King of Fighters yet, now’s the time!

notes.title: King of Fighters 15 open beta set for November
notes.notes:
King of Fighters 15 gets an open beta in November.

The open beta test, which was announced for PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 during tonight's Sony State of Play broadcast, kicks off on 20th November and runs until 22nd November. It includes eight playable characters, and lets you play online casual matches and online room matches. There's offline training, too.

notes.title: King of Fighters 15 out February 2022
notes.notes:
King of Fighters 15 comes out 17th February 2022.

The announcement was made in a new video shown off during the Gamescom Opening Night Live pre-show. The video, below, confirms 39 playable characters and the return of the series' classic 3v3 battle system.

SNK fighting game King of Fighters 15 is due out on PC via the Epic Games Store and Steam, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 4, Xbox Series X and S and Xbox One.

notes.title: Gamescom 2021 schedule guide: All gamescom conference dates and times explained
notes.notes:
As with E3 2021, gamescom once again opts for an all digital showing this year.

Alongside some week-long programming from event organisers themselves - including a headline stream hosted by Geoff Keighley of The Game Awards fame, and an indie-focused showcase - you can expect a dedicated show from Xbox and another Future Games Show later in the week.

Though busier than last year's show, it's still more subdued than the gamescom we've come to know over the years - but at least, like E3, 2021's conferences are condensed into a single week than a seemingly never-ending list of streams over the summer. Phew!
